bib.title: Open Deep Search: Democratizing Search with Open-source Reasoning Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Open Deep Search: Democratizing Search with Open-source Reasoning Agents", Alzubi, Brooks, Chiniya, Contente, von Gerlach, Irwin, Jiang, Kaz, Nguyen, Oh, Tyagi, Viswanath (Sentient; UW; Princeton; UC Berkeley). arXiv:2503.20201v1 [cs.LG], 26 Mar 2025. Preprint; no venue printed.

COVERAGE: all 27 pages read, 103,178 chars. Pages 1-12 main text; 13-14 references; 15-19 appendix A (example responses, skimmed); 20-27 appendix B (20 few-shot ReAct examples, skimmed) and appendix C (related work). Extraction clean.

NOTE-MISMATCH CHECK: The note's numbers match the paper. DeepSeek-R1 alone 82.4 (SimpleQA) / 30.1 (FRAMES); ODS with R1 88.3 / 75.3. The 88.3/75.3 figures are ODS-v2 (CodeAct), not ODS-v1. Only mismatch risk: the note and references.md should say "ODS-v2 + DeepSeek-R1". ODS-v1+R1 is 87.7 / 56.7. Also note the paper's SimpleQA numbers are self-run (see Table 3 asterisks).

CLAIMS
1. ODS-v2 + DeepSeek-R1 gets 88.3% SimpleQA and 75.3% FRAMES, versus bare R1 at 82.4% and 30.1%.
 number: 88.3 / 75.3 vs 82.4 / 30.1
 setup: Table 1. Base LLM DeepSeek-R1; ODS-v2 uses a CodeAct agent (smolagents CodeAgent). Full SimpleQA (4326 q), FRAMES (824 q). Bare R1 has no web access.
 quote: "ODS-v1+DeepSeek-R1 (ours) 87.7 56.7 / ODS-v2+DeepSeek-R1 (ours) 88.3 75.3" and "DeepSeek-R1 82.4 30.1"; abstract: "DeepSeek-R1 that achieves 82.4% on SimpleQA and 30.1% on FRAMES—with search and reasoning capabilities to achieve state-of-the-art performance: 88.3% on SimpleQA and 75.3% on FRAMES."
 where: p.1 abstract, p.2 Table 1
2. Table 1 baselines (SimpleQA / FRAMES). Without web: Llama3.1-70B 20.4 / 34.3; DeepSeek-R1 82.4 / 30.1; GPT-4o 37.5 / 50.5. With web: Perplexity 82.4 / 42.4; Perplexity Sonar Reasoning Pro 85.8 / 44.4; GPT-4o Search Preview 90.0 / 65.6; ODS-v1+R1 87.7 / 56.7; ODS-v2+R1 88.3 / 75.3.
 quote: "GPT-4o Search Preview [17] 90.0 65.6" ; "Perplexity Sonar Reasoning Pro [22] 85.8 44.4" ; "Perplexity [21] 82.4 42.4"
 where: p.2 Table 1
3. ODS-v2 beats GPT-4o Search Preview on FRAMES but trails on SimpleQA. Abstract says +9.7% accuracy (75.3-65.6); conclusion says "by 10%". Both are absolute points.
 quote: "ODS improves the best existing baseline of the recently released GPT-4o Search Preview by 9.7% in accuracy." ; "Compared to GPT-4o Search Preview, ODS-v2 has a significantly better FRAMES accuracy but a slightly worse SimpleQA accuracy."
 where: p.1, p.2, p.12
4. ODS-v2 searches adaptively: 3.39 searches per query on FRAMES, 1.45 on SimpleQA. ODS-v1+R1 always does 1.00. Weaker Llama3.1-70B under ODS-v1 searches more.
 setup: Table 2, averages per query.
 quote: "ODS-v1+Llama3.1-70B 83.4 49.5 1.09 1.05 / ODS-v1+DeepSeek-R1 87.7 56.7 1.00 1.00 / ODS-v2+DeepSeek-R1 88.3 75.3 1.45 3.39"
 where: p.8 Table 2
5. Ablation (ODS-v1, Table 4; SimpleQA on a random 500-question subset, FRAMES full). Llama3.1-70B alone 21.2 / 34.3. Adding Open Search Tool gives 82.4 / 27.6 (FRAMES drops). Adding CoT-ReAct gives 87.2 / 37.4. Adding FewShot gives 87.8 / 49.5. Swapping to DeepSeek-R1 gives 90.4 / 56.7.
 quote: "OpenSearchTool + Llama3.1-70B 82.4 27.6" ; "OpenSearchTool + DeepSeek-R1 + CoT-ReAct + FewShot 90.4 56.7"
 where: p.9 text, p.11 Table 4
6. Single-search FRAMES comparison: the best single-query baseline in the FRAMES paper is Gemini-Pro-1.5-0514 at 47.4% with 4 retrieved docs (BM25). ODS-v1+R1 reaches 56.7% with one search. Gemini needs about 15 rephrased searches to get similar performance.
 quote: "The best single-query search approach reported in [8] achieves a score of 47.4% with Gemini-Pro-1.5-0514"
 where: p.7-8
7. Table 3 SimpleQA survey. Open-source: DeepSeek-R1 82.4, DeepSeek-V3 24.9, Qwen 2.5 9.1, ODS-v2+R1 88.3* (* = run by the authors). Closed-source higher than ODS: GPT-4o Search Preview 90.0, Exa 90.0, Linkup 90.1, Perplexity Deep Research 93.9. Perplexity Sonar 77.3. Others are copied from cited sources, not rerun.
 quote: "Perplexity Deep Research [23] 93.9" ; "Table 3: ODS-v2 achieves the best accuracy on SimpleQA among open-source solutions.∗ indicates evaluations run by us."
 where: p.11
8. SimpleQA judge is GPT-4o-mini (LLM-as-judge). The paper reports no FRAMES judge.
 quote: "An LLM-as-a-judge with GPT-4o-mini is used to check for correctness"
 where: p.8

ARCHITECTURE (for the note)
- Open Search Tool: (1) query rephrasing into k queries; (2) SERP retrieval via serper.dev, FreshPrompt-style formatting (title, URL, description, date), prompt tells LLM to prefer government, educational and research sources on conflict; (3) augmentation: scrape top m links, embed passage chunks, keep top n passages per page by re-ranker score. The intro adds a relevance threshold and custom handling for Wikipedia, ArXiv and PubMed. The paper names no embedding or reranker model.
 quote: "we rephrase queries when necessary, extract context from the top N snippets, and apply chunking and re-ranking to filter content above a relevance threshold." (p.2)
- ODS-v1: CoT + ReAct + dynamic few-shot (vector-similarity picks examples from 200 community-written ReAct prompts). Tools: search, Wolfram Alpha calculator, "continue thinking". Fallback: when a Llama-3-8B judge decides ReAct failed, run CoT self-consistency (r samples, cluster, pick from the largest cluster).
- ODS-v2: smolagents CodeAgent (CodeAct variant), Python code as the action format. Tools: search, calculator, reflection, Python interpreter.
- Plug-and-play base LLM. Tested only with Llama3.1-70B and DeepSeek-R1.

LIMITS
- There is no limitations section. The authors concede closed-source systems (GPT-4o Search Preview, Exa, Linkup, Perplexity Deep Research) "claim to achieve higher SimpleQA scores".
- Internal inconsistencies: ODS-v1+Llama3.1-70B SimpleQA is 83.4 in Table 2 but 84.0 in Table 3. Intro text says "ODS-v1... leverages OpenPerplex" for search, while Section 2.1 says serper.dev. The text says ODS-v2+R1 is "version one of ODS" in one place (typo, p.3). Fig 3 caption says Perplexity answered 79; the Perplexity response shows no definite answer.
- Appendix A example mislabels the Jensen question as FRAMES in the appendix while the main text labels it SimpleQA.
- Baselines are closed APIs and were not re-evaluated for Sonar, Exa, etc. in Table 3. Table 1 numbers for Perplexity and GPT-4o Search Preview are apparently authors' runs (no asterisk in Table 1).
- Ablation SimpleQA is a 500-question subset only.
- No cost, latency, variance or seed information. No statistical tests. No run-to-run variation reported.
- FRAMES here is used with web access rather than the original Wikipedia-given setup.
- Dated: March 2025 snapshot (GPT-4o Search Preview released 3/11/2025); later deep-research systems are not covered.

BUILDS ON: FreshLLMs / FreshPrompt (Vu et al. 2023); ReAct (Yao et al. 2022, printed as Yao, Zhao, Yu, Du, Shafran, Narasimhan, Cao); Chain-of-Thought (Wei et al. 2022); zero-shot CoT (Kojima et al. 2022); CoT self-consistency (Wang et al. 2022); Chain-of-Code (Li et al. 2024); CodeAct (printed as Lv, Xia, Huang 2024; the cited paper is the arXiv 2408 entry); smolagents (Roucher et al. 2025); FRAMES (Krishna et al. 2024); SimpleQA (Wei et al. 2024); DeepSeek-R1 (Guo et al. 2025); RAG (Lewis et al. 2020); open search tools OpenPerplex and Perplexica.

CODE: none beyond the ReAct tag format (p.5, Figure 2): <Question> ... <Thought> ... <Action>search_internet</Action> <Action_Input> ... <Observation> ... <Final_Answer>. Repo: https://github.com/sentient-agi/OpenDeepSearch (p.3).

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.3): architecture, query to Open Reasoning Agent to tools (Open Search Tool, code interpreter, calculator, think) to output.
- Fig 5 (p.8): histogram of number of searches by ODS-v2, fewer on SimpleQA than FRAMES. Shows adaptive search effort.
- Figs 3, 6, 7, 8 (pp.6, 9, 10): worked answer examples against Perplexity.
Figures were not extracted with the script; captions taken from the text.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Layout of tables is flattened but readable. Figure 4 (CodeAct trace) has no text caption content beyond "CodeAct agent in ODS-v2 answering a multi-hop question."
